root.name: Benoni Defense: Woozle
root.moves: 1. d4 c5 2. d5 Nf6 3. Nc3 Qa5

overview: Black answers 2.d5 Nf6 3.Nc3 with 3...Qa5, an early queen sortie that pins or eyes the c3 knight and the e1 square. White has a space edge with d5 and can drive the queen back with Bd2 or e4. Neither side has any forcing theory.

white_ideas.idea: Gain time against the queen with Bd2 and Nf3
Build a centre with e4 and use the space

black_ideas.idea: Harass the knight on c3 and prepare ...b5 or ...e6
Use the queen to put pressure on c3 and a2

typical_structures.structure: Benoni-like pawn chain with d5 against c5
Closed centre with the Black queen on a5

character.notes: Quiet, offbeat play with the queen out early; nothing is forced.

soundness.notes: Black loses time with the queen but there is no immediate refutation.

structure.notes: Pawn chain d5/c5 with a tense centre.

approach.notes: Strong players hardly play this queen sortie.

level.notes: Little theory to learn, mostly a surprise.

sublines_that_differ.name: 4.Bd2
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. d4 c5 2. d5 Nf6 3. Nc3 Qa5 4. Bd2
sublines_that_differ.how: Quiet reply that gains a tempo on the queen.

character.reason: The line has no sharp theory but is not especially solid either.

soundness.reason: The early queen loses time but White has no forced punishment.

structure.reason: The centre is undecided with d5 and c5 in contact.

approach.reason: Strong players seldom play this queen move.

level.reason: There is little to memorise and the plans are not hard.

plans.reason: The queen comes out early and White has more space.
